subject: Phased uplift, slab pricing and true-up path for renewal
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cascadelabs.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@cascadelabs.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — handling mid-contract growth and uplift

Hi Rishi,

Quick note as we start planning for our July renewal. Cascade's usage is trending up — about 28% q/q for the last two quarters — and the finance team is nervous about a big one-time uplift. We want an approach that smooths the uplift into our renewal while keeping unit economics predictable.

Specifically, can Redwood propose a path that:
- Splits the uplift across a few billing slabs (quarterly or bi-annual) rather than a single immediate top-up
- Provides a short true-up window for unexpected burst months
- Keeps an option to co-term with our other vendor contracts in Oct 2027

Attached is our current consumption export and a short summary. We're open to a modest multi-quarter discount in exchange for committing to a stepped slab.

Thanks — can you sketch a recommended structure and the impact on monthly invoices? We need this for our internal renewal deck by next Monday.

Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
Cascade Labs

Attachments: cascade-usage-may2027.csv (csv), cascade-renewal-notes.docx (docx)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cascadelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — handling mid-contract growth and uplift

Alex — thanks for the detail and the attachments. High level proposal below; I put Ben and Tessa on copy for quoting/ops and looped Kim for billing cadence.

Proposal: "Phased Slab Uplift" (summary)
- Commit slabs: create 3 slabs for the 12-month renewal: Base (current committed), Slab A (25% incremental), Slab B (50% incremental).
- Phased billing: move Slab A into effect at renewal month, Slab B phases in 3 months later if usage trend persists. Each slab has its own per-token unit rate (slab pricing), with higher volumes in later slabs receiving a modest step-down.
- True-up window: 60-day rolling true-up to reconcile bursts; excess beyond slab ceilings billed at on-demand rate but eligible for a one-time migration credit if sustained >90 days.
- Discount ladder: 5% blended discount on Slab A for committing to a 12-month stepped plan; additional 3% if Cascade agrees to a co-term with the Oct 2027 enterprise bundle.

Why this helps
- Smooths invoice shock — spreads uplift into Slab A and B rather than a single top-up.
- Preserves predictability — true-up window reduces surprise billing while still protecting Redwood capacity.
- Gives Cascade runway to decide on co-term without locking full uplift immediately.

Operational asks
1) Confirmation of slab sizes (we propose 25% and 50% above current commit).
2) Approval to include a one-time migration credit (we recommend a $12k credit against the first true-up invoice if Slab B is triggered).
3) Target co-term decision by Sept 1 to realize the extra 3% discount on Slab B.

I've attached a simple slab-pricing model that shows monthly invoice scenarios under conservative/expected/aggressive growth. Ben — can you produce a formal quote matrix and payment terms?

Next step: I'll draft a renewal amendment (short form) that captures slabs, true-up language, and credit. If Cascade is aligned, we can issue a formal quote and PO path this week.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: slab-pricing-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — handling mid-contract growth and uplift

Rishi — quick note, I like the phased slabs. Two tweaks from a commercial ops perspective:

- Raise the one-time migration credit to $18k if Cascade signs the 12-month stepped commit by June 20; it helps get finance comfortable and still nets out at our expected ARR impact.
- For invoicing, propose invoicing Slab A immediately at renewal pro rata; Slab B billed only once usage crosses the slab threshold for two consecutive months (gives them a buffer and reduces disputes).

Alex — if that's workable I can run the quote with legal and include sample SOW language for the 60-day true-up and the migration credit trigger.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
